## generic_band_dock_gen1

**No issue found in the bounded audit.** The selected source is SHA-256 `1b0ace7af5266241c7e68fc601a522d36a48f3e159faa4a08361bfd230c9430d`, identical to the catalog's reviewed source hash. I generated 10 seeds in each of easy, medium, and hard (30 tasks, 130 total train/test pairs). Every task passed the generator's observational `self_check_task`, repeated generation was byte-identical, and each training lesson covered both orientations and both docking sides. Evidence: `checks/audit/generic_band_dock_gen1/probe.py` and `checks/audit/generic_band_dock_gen1/probe-results.json`.

I also inspected the selected rule, declared rivals, construction-time detector check, and three-example training plan for first-fit ambiguity or an uncovered orientation/side branch. I did not find a concrete counterexample. The public one-grid `arcpuzzles apply` command cannot independently replay a generic task because it requires a resolvable per-puzzle canonical rule; that failed probe is retained at `checks/audit/generic_band_dock_gen1/public-apply-attempt.log`. Therefore this clean audit is finite and does not independently re-prove the inherited 520-pair Racket-parity claim.
